submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 with a threshold of 32.5 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency of 93.06% at the allocated 8 kHz rate. This significantly outperforms Algorithm-L3 (best: ~86.7% at 35 GeV) and Algorithm-L2 (best: ~73% at 30-35 GeV). The iterative topological clustering with learned calibration (Algorithm-L1) provides superior performance compared to the fixed-window sum (L2) and sliding-window clustering (L3) approaches. The threshold of 32.5 GeV was determined through systematic optimization, testing various values within the 20-60 GeV range. This configuration maximizes physics reach while meeting all deployment constraints.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) is one of the three candidates specified in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware
requirements.evidence: According to candidate_specs.md, all three algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs). According to links.md, the 25 Gb/s links have enough bandwidth for all candidate algorithms. Therefore Algorithm-L1 is deployable.
The recommended threshold of 32.5 GeV is within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Through systematic simulation, Algorithm-L1 at 32.5 GeV achieves 93.06% signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate, which is the highest among all tested configurations. This exceeds Algorithm-L3 (best: 86.7%) and Algorithm-L2 (best: 73%).
